answer: An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the spiral check immediately, the ledge audit keeps the resolved set and the dawn replay shows exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 288 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 288 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
